Found via homepage nav: 'Best Sellers' -> /pplp/cat-387851.aspx. SCOPE DECISION: SR278 'La Redoute Interiors UK' is specifically the 'La Redoute Interieurs' (LRI) HOME-ONLY house-brand/collection line, not the general fashion+home retailer (that is SR82 'La Redoute UK', same domain). Confirmed via the LRI brand microsite's own nav (brnd/la-redoute-interieurs.aspx), which lists only home/interiors categories (Furniture, Lighting, Tableware, Bedroom & Bedding, Tables & Chairs, Rugs & Runners, Garden, Sofas & Armchairs, Home Furnishings & Textiles, Home Accessories & Decor, DIY) and zero fashion/clothing categories. BRAND-FILTER CHECK: there is no separate LRI-scoped Bestsellers entry point anywhere -- the LRI brand page nav has no 'Bestsellers' link, and the Best Sellers hub/children are general sitewide listings not filterable by brndid (confirmed: appending ?brndid=la-redoute-interieurs to /pplp/cat-387851.aspx still returned the Cloudflare challenge, i.e. no brand-specific variant exists to even test). DUPLICATE-VS-SR82 DETERMINATION (for orchestrator): for the 9 home-department rows below, SR278 and SR82 read the exact same URLs with the exact same counts -- there is no LRI-specific filtering available for Bestsellers. So these 9 rows are not unique LRI data; they are the subset of SR82's full (fashion+home) Bestsellers output that falls in home/interiors. Orchestrator should decide whether to keep both (SR278 as an explicit home-only cross-reference) or treat SR278 as redundant with SR82's home rows -- do not treat SR278 as introducing a brand-filtered COUNT distinct from SR82's for this concept, unlike the Category-taxonomy project where LRI genuinely had its own filtered subset.
